question: Do modern image generators make systematic projective-geometry and illumination errors that remain detectable after ordinary pixel-level forensic cues fail?

key_findings.claim: The study isolates three derived geometry channels—perspective fields, line segments, and object-shadow masks—and denies the final classifiers access to RGB pixels.
key_findings.evidence: Perspective and object-shadow representations are classified with ResNet50, while unordered DeepLSD line segments are processed by a PointNet-like model; all inputs are produced by pretrained geometry extractors.

key_findings.claim: A pixel ResNet prequalifier deliberately selects generated and real images that are difficult or inverted for conventional signal detection.
key_findings.evidence: Separate indoor, outdoor, and combined prequalifiers are trained on real images and four generators. Evaluation emphasizes unconfident sets where prequalifier AUC is about 0.49-0.51 and misclassified sets where it is 0.00.

key_findings.claim: Geometry-only classifiers separate real and generated images even on the hard prequalified subsets.
key_findings.evidence: Across scene types and cues, reported AUCs range from 0.72 to 0.97. On unconfident subsets, examples include 0.82 for indoor lines, 0.84 for outdoor perspective, and 0.80 for combined perspective and shadows; misclassified subsets reach up to 0.82.

key_findings.claim: Geometry detectors trained on Kandinsky generalize to several unseen open and proprietary generators and image composites.
key_findings.evidence: Cross-generator ROC analyses include Stable Diffusion XL, DeepFloyd IF, PixArt-alpha, DALL-E 3, Adobe Firefly, and a recent compositing method, with qualitative Grad-CAM examples marking shadow and vanishing-point failures.

key_findings.claim: Line and perspective cues are correlated, while shadow cues add complementary failure evidence.
key_findings.evidence: Supplementary Table 2 reports a highly significant association between line and perspective decisions and a distinct, lower-frequency object-shadow pattern; Grad-CAM examples likewise show cases accepted by one cue and rejected by another.

key_findings.claim: The experiment demonstrates a detectable distribution difference, not that generators possess no projective representation or that detected errors are measured against ground-truth scene geometry.
key_findings.evidence: All geometry channels are predictions from learned extractors, labels are real versus generated rather than calibrated vanishing points or light sources, and classifiers can exploit extractor-domain biases. Grad-CAM is suggestive but does not validate a physical rule per example.

method.core_idea: Filter away easy RGB artifacts, then test whether learned abstractions of long-range perspective and lighting still distinguish synthetic from real images.
method.mechanism: Real-image captions prompt multiple generators. A pixel classifier partitions evaluation into easy, uncertain, and wrong cases. Separate classifiers learn from predicted perspective vector fields, detected line sets, or binary object-shadow associations, and cross-generator evaluation tests whether geometry failures transfer.
assumptions: The pretrained geometry extractors respond comparably to real and synthetic images except for genuine geometry differences.
Prequalification removes rather than merely changes low-level shortcuts.
Real web and dataset images provide an appropriate distribution of physically plausible projective geometry.
A real-versus-generated classifier score reflects geometry validity rather than generator-specific semantic composition.

techniques.role: Constructs uncertain and deliberately misclassified subsets for conventional forensic features.
Classifies local up-vector and latitude fields predicted from each image.
Detects anomalous global line arrangements without raster intensity.
Tests relative position and shape patterns of detected objects and shadows.
Trains on one generator and evaluates multiple unseen generator families.

evaluations.setting: LSUN indoor and BDD100K/Mapillary outdoor real images paired by caption with Kandinsky, SDXL, DeepFloyd IF, and PixArt-alpha outputs.
evaluations.metric: ROC AUC on easy, recent-timestamp, pixel-unconfident, and pixel-misclassified subsets.
evaluations.result: Three geometry-only channels obtain 0.72-0.97 AUC overall and remain substantially above chance on hard subsets.
evaluations.baseline: RGB ResNet50 prequalifier and simple geometry-cue statistics.

evaluations.setting: Kandinsky-trained geometry classifiers evaluated on unseen open and proprietary generators.
evaluations.metric: Cross-generator ROC AUC and qualitative saliency localization.
evaluations.result: Detectors transfer to SDXL, DeepFloyd, PixArt, DALL-E 3, and Firefly, with saliency often on distorted building lines, road markings, or shadows.
evaluations.baseline: State-of-the-art local signal detectors referenced by the paper.

evaluations.setting: Agreement analysis among line, perspective, and shadow decisions on SDXL hard examples.
evaluations.metric: Joint detection frequencies and association test.
evaluations.result: Lines and perspective overlap strongly; object-shadow detections are less frequent and complementary.

limitations: Geometry labels are indirect real/generated labels rather than ground-truth vanishing points, camera calibration, or illumination parameters.
All final inputs depend on pretrained learned extractors that may carry their own domain and rendering biases.
Data curation and captions do not guarantee matched scene complexity, object count, or photographic post-processing.
Detection results can decay as generators improve or adapt against the known cues.
The study evaluates still-image scene categories and does not establish temporal, multi-view, or 3D consistency.
failure_modes: A geometry extractor may fail differently on synthetic texture and create a spurious downstream cue.
Stylized or deliberately impossible real photographs may be falsely labeled generated.
Simple synthetic scenes with few lines, objects, or shadows provide insufficient evidence.
Generator-specific prompt composition can change the distribution of geometry even when each rendered relation is valid.
Adversarial correction of vanishing points and shadows may defeat detection without improving other physical inconsistencies.
reusable_insights: Evaluate generators through derived, interpretable physical abstractions after filtering easy pixel artifacts.
Use complementary long-range cues because perspective and illumination fail in different images.
Cross-generator and recent-real tests are essential for separating source artifacts from broader synthetic regularities.
Distinguish forensic separability from calibrated physical correctness.
open_questions: How much AUC remains when geometry extractors are validated against human or synthetic ground truth on both domains?
Can explicit projective and illumination constraints repair generation rather than only detect it?
Do the same cues predict failures in video and multi-view 3D generation?
How quickly do geometry detectors become obsolete as generator architectures and training data change?

competitive_landscape.title: DIRE for Diffusion-Generated Image Detection
competitive_landscape.relationship: Strong cross-diffusion forensic detector based on reconstruction error.
competitive_landscape.difference: DIRE exploits a diffusion model's reconstruction signature in pixel space; this paper intentionally filters such signal cues and classifies only derived long-range geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: GenImage: A Million-Scale Benchmark for Detecting AI-Generated Image
competitive_landscape.relationship: Large benchmark for generator and degradation generalization in synthetic-image detection.
competitive_landscape.difference: GenImage measures generic forensic classifiers over many sources; the projective-geometry study narrows the hypothesis to interpretable line, perspective, and shadow channels on prequalified hard cases.

competitive_landscape.title: Perspective Fields for Single Image Camera Calibration
competitive_landscape.relationship: Primary geometry representation and extractor used for one detector channel.
competitive_landscape.difference: Perspective Fields estimates camera geometry for calibration and compositing; this paper classifies its predicted fields to diagnose systematic errors in generated scenes.

competitive_landscape.title: ControlVP: Interactive Geometric Refinement of AI-Generated Images with Consistent Vanishing Points
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later adjacent work directly correcting the vanishing-point failure identified here.
competitive_landscape.difference: ControlVP adds user-guided structural constraints during refinement; this paper provides a multi-cue forensic diagnosis but does not modify generation.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Modern generators systematically violate projective and shadow geometry, and those violations enable robust detection even when pixel forensics fail.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The hard-set curation and three pixel-denied channels provide unusually direct evidence for cross-generator geometric distribution shifts. The provocative 'do not know geometry' wording is stronger than the experiment: learned extractors and binary source labels do not establish internal knowledge or per-image physical ground truth.

reviewer_notes: Read all 23 extracted pages, including curation counts, three derived channels, every hard-set and cross-generator result, cue agreement, recent-image tests, and supplementary distributions. Current primary arXiv neighbors, including later geometric correction work, were checked on 2026-08-23.
